roleFlavor.responder: The Naruto creator and TV Tokyo guard the brand and look for a fair share.

howItWorks: Sekai offers a contract with payment and creative control details.
The creator and TV Tokyo review the offer and can ask for changes.
Both sides see each other's proposals at the same time.
If they agree, the card game can be released. If not, the deal falls apart.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Choose the final terms of the agreement

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The contract is signed. The game launches and both parties share the profits.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side pulls out. The game never launches and both lose potential earnings.
outcomes.MIXED: They reach a partial agreement. The game launches with limited features, giving modest returns to both.

items.headline: Travelodge CEO Exits After Mishandling of Guest’s Sexual Assault Case
items.facts: Travelodge CEO Jo Boydell resigned after pressure over the group’s handling of a sexual assault case.

framing.narrativeTitle: Jo Boydell Steps Down from Travelodge
framing.publicBrief: Travelodge group faces a storm after a guest reported sexual assault. The case drew angry headlines. Stakeholders in the hotel industry press the chain for a clear response. Jo Boydell, the chief executive, steps down as pressure mounts. The group must decide how to rebuild trust while the industry watches.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Jo Boydell, the departing CEO, holding the power to shape the company’s next move.
roleFlavor.responder: You are the industry stakeholders, watching Travelodge and ready to judge its actions.

howItWorks: Each side makes a single offer.
The other side can accept or reject it.
If the offer is accepted, the deal goes through.
If it is rejected, both sides walk away.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: What will each side propose?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Travelodge and the industry agree on a plan, restoring confidence.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side refuses the other's terms, deepening the crisis.
outcomes.MIXED: A partial agreement is reached, leaving some issues unresolved.

items.headline: FCC officially decides gigabit speeds are too good for you
items.facts: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr decided to cancel long‑term broadband speed goals, ending the push for gigabit downloads.

framing.narrativeTitle: FCC Cancels Gigabit Goals
framing.publicBrief: It is evening at the Federal Communications Commission. Chairman Brendan Carr has made his decision. He cancels the long-term goal for gigabit broadband speeds. This ends the push for faster internet access for all Americans. The telecom industry supports this move. They do not want strict speed targets. The public loses a promise of better service. The deal is final. The rules are gone.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. You hold the power to set national rules. You can choose to keep the speed goals or cancel them. Your choice ends the debate.
roleFlavor.responder: You represent the telecom industry. You want no strict speed targets. You prefer to set your own pace for upgrades. You accept the cancellation as a win.

howItWorks: Brendan Carr makes the final decision on broadband goals.
The telecom industry reacts to his choice.
If he keeps the goals, the industry must comply.
If he cancels them, the industry is free to act.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: What does Brendan Carr decide?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Goals kept. Industry complies. Public gets faster internet promises.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Goals cancelled. Industry wins. Public loses the promise of speed.
outcomes.MIXED: Partial deal. Some goals remain. Industry faces some rules.

items.headline: How Florida quietly removed climate change content from textbooks
items.facts: Florida state requested publishers to dilute climate change content; publishers complied, altering textbook language.

framing.narrativeTitle: Florida State and Publishers Swap Words on Climate
framing.publicBrief: Florida state asked publishers to soften climate change talk in school books. Publishers changed the words to meet the request. The state keeps the new text, the publishers keep the rest of the book.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Florida state. You want the books to say less about climate change.
roleFlavor.responder: You are Publishers. You want to keep the original words but must obey the state.

howItWorks: Florida state tells publishers what to say in the books.
Publishers can choose to follow the request or refuse.
If they follow, the books change and Florida keeps the new text.
If they refuse, the books stay the same but Florida may act against them.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will the publishers change the words?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Publishers changed the words. Florida keeps the new text.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Publishers kept the original words. Florida may act against them.
outcomes.MIXED: Publishers partially changed the words. Florida keeps the new text.

items.headline: The Dinner Party Has Left the Building
items.facts: Artists created a dinner setting on a natural rock by a waterfall and invited diners to eat there.

framing.narrativeTitle: The Dinner by the Falls
framing.publicBrief: Charles Michel set a table on a rock by a waterfall. He invited diners to eat there. The water rushes around the stone. The air is cool and wet. It is night. The table is ready. The food is hot. The diners must decide if they will come. They can stay home for safety. Or they can join him for the meal. The lights are low. The sound of water is loud.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are part of the group invited to eat. You hold your place at the table. You risk the wet rocks. You see the fire and the food if you come.

STAG.label: JOIN THE MEAL
STAG.meaning: Walk to the rock and sit down.
STAG.outcome: You eat the feast together. The night is a success.

HARE.label: STAY HOME
HARE.outcome: You stay dry and safe. The table remains empty.

howItWorks: Both guests choose at the same time. Neither can see the other. If both join, the party happens. If both stay, nothing happens.
If one joins and the other stays, the guest who joins is left alone. The guest who stays is safe but misses out. Coming together gives the best result.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will you sit at the table?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The feast is shared. Everyone eats well.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One person is alone in the dark. The other is safe.
outcomes.MIXED: The table is empty. The food goes cold.
